subtopic_detail: Loose soiling most days of the week in a well grown six year old who opens his bowels fully only every eight to ten days
stem:
You are the paediatric registrar in a general outpatient clinic seeing a six year old boy whose parents have brought him because he has been soiling his underwear four or five days a week for three months. They describe the soiling as loose and runny and think he has ongoing diarrhoea, and his teacher has twice sent him home from school.

He opens his bowels fully into the toilet about once every eight to ten days, and his mother says those motions are so large they block the toilet. He passed meconium on the first day of life and his weight and height have tracked along the 50th centile throughout. His lower back and neurological examination are normal, and his abdomen is soft with a firm mass palpable in the left iliac fossa. His general practitioner prescribed a fixed low dose stool softener which the family gave for four weeks without any change.

data_table.Examination: Abdomen soft with a firm non tender mass in the left iliac fossa, normal perianal appearance and anal position, normal lower back with no sacral dimple or hair tuft, normal lower limb tone power and reflexes
data_table.Growth: Weight and height both on the 50th centile with no change in centile over two years

lead_in: What is the most appropriate next step in his management?

options.text: Arrange an abdominal radiograph to confirm the extent of faecal loading
options.rationale: A radiograph adds nothing when a faecal mass is already palpable, and radiographic loading scores correlate poorly with the clinical picture, so it delivers radiation without changing the plan. Imaging is reserved for genuine diagnostic doubt or a suspected obstructive complication (Source: RCH CPG: Constipation).

options.text: Refer for a rectal suction biopsy to exclude an aganglionic segment
options.rationale: The condition this test looks for declares itself with meconium passage beyond 48 hours, poor growth and a narrow empty rectum that decompresses explosively on examination, none of which fit a child on the 50th centile who passed meconium on day one. Overflow soiling is in fact distinctly uncommon in aganglionosis, which argues against it rather than for it (Source: RCH CPG: Constipation).

options.text: Start an escalating oral macrogol regimen with a scheduled toileting plan
options.rationale: Runny soiling with infrequent enormous stools and a palpable faecal mass is overflow around a retained load, and no maintenance dose will work until that load is cleared, which an escalating macrogol course achieves at home over three to seven days. Pairing it with sitting on the toilet after meals treats the withholding behaviour that keeps the cycle going (Source: RCH CPG: Constipation).

options.text: Give a phosphate enema now before starting any maintenance treatment
options.rationale: Rectal disimpaction sits second in the Australian sequence because oral macrogol clears the same load without a rectal procedure in a child who is already withholding, and paediatric phosphate enemas can cause hyperphosphataemia with hypocalcaemia. It becomes reasonable only after an adequate oral course has failed (Source: Therapeutic Guidelines: Gastrointestinal).

options.text: Prescribe a daily stimulant laxative alone and review him in six weeks
options.rationale: A stimulant without a disimpaction phase repeats the mistake of the earlier fixed low dose trial, because driving peristalsis against an impacted rectum increases the soiling and the pain that reinforces withholding. Stimulants earn their place added to maintenance macrogol once the load has cleared (Source: Therapeutic Guidelines: Gastrointestinal).

explanation.summary: Functional constipation accounts for more than 95 per cent of childhood constipation and the diagnosis is clinical, resting on stool frequency, calibre, withholding behaviour and an abdominal or rectal faecal mass. Soiling in this setting is almost always overflow rather than true diarrhoea, and families and schools routinely misread it as a behavioural problem or gastroenteritis. Treatment has two distinct phases that are frequently collapsed into one: clearing the retained load, then a maintenance dose continued long enough for a stretched rectum to regain sensation. Red flags that shift the workup are delayed meconium, failure to thrive, bilious vomiting, an abnormal sacral or neurological examination and onset in the first month of life. Relapse is the norm when maintenance is stopped as soon as things improve.
key_points: Runny soiling with infrequent large stools is overflow around a retained faecal load
Disimpaction must precede maintenance or the maintenance dose appears to fail
Oral macrogol is first line for disimpaction in Australia, ahead of rectal treatment
Radiographs correlate poorly with clinical constipation and are not needed to diagnose it
Passage of meconium on day one with normal growth argues strongly against aganglionosis
explanation.pearls: Macrogol 3350 with electrolytes is titrated up daily over three to seven days for disimpaction, then continued at a maintenance dose for at least two months after a soft daily stool is established, because stopping as soon as the soiling settles is the single commonest reason it comes back.

subtopic_detail: Itch of the palms and soles without a rash at 34 weeks with a raised serum bile acid level
stem:
You are the obstetric registrar reviewing a 29 year old woman in her first pregnancy at 34 weeks and two days. For the past twelve days she has had itching that is worst in the evening and overnight, mainly on her palms and the soles of her feet, and she has been scratching until she bleeds.

Her skin shows excoriation marks over her forearms and shins but no primary rash, and there are no lesions in the abdominal striae. Her blood pressure is 112/68 mmHg and her urine dipstick shows no protein. Her serum bile acids taken non fasting are 42 micromol/L with an alanine aminotransferase of 96 U/L, and her full blood count, coagulation profile and hepatitis and viral serology are all within normal limits. A liver ultrasound shows no gallstones and normal ducts. The foetus is growing along the 40th centile with a normal cardiotocograph.

data_table.Vital signs: Pulse rate 82 per minute, blood pressure 112/68 mmHg, respiratory rate 16 per minute, SpO2 99 per cent, temperature 36.7 degrees C, foetal heart rate 142 per minute
data_table.Investigations: Serum bile acids 42 micromol/L (less than 19), alanine aminotransferase 96 U/L (less than 35), bilirubin 12 micromol/L (less than 20), platelets 244 x10^9/L (150-400), prothrombin time within normal limits, viral hepatitis serology negative
data_table.Imaging: Liver ultrasound with no gallstones and normal intrahepatic and extrahepatic ducts

lead_in: What is the most appropriate plan for the remainder of her pregnancy?

options.text: Repeat bile acid levels weekly and plan birth at 38 to 39 weeks gestation
options.rationale: The excess perinatal risk in this condition tracks with the peak bile acid concentration, and levels below 100 micromol/L carry a stillbirth rate close to the background population rate, so birth is planned at 38 to 39 weeks rather than earlier. Serial levels matter because a rise into the severe range shifts that plan forward (Source: RANZCOG: Obstetric cholestasis).

options.text: Arrange birth by caesarean section within 48 hours given the stillbirth risk
options.rationale: Immediate birth at 34 weeks trades a very small excess stillbirth risk at this bile acid level for the certain respiratory and neurodevelopmental costs of late preterm delivery, and the mode of birth is not itself altered by the diagnosis. Urgent birth belongs to levels of 100 micromol/L or more with other complicating features (Source: RANZCOG: Obstetric cholestasis).

options.text: Start weekly cardiotocography and continue the pregnancy to 41 weeks gestation
options.rationale: Cardiotocography and ultrasound surveillance do not predict the sudden foetal demise associated with this condition, which is thought to be an arrhythmic event rather than a progressive hypoxic one, so normal traces provide false reassurance. Expectant management to 41 weeks also abandons the timing benefit that drives the whole plan (Source: RANZCOG: Obstetric cholestasis).

options.text: Give betamethasone now and plan induction of labour at 36 weeks gestation
options.rationale: Birth at 36 weeks is reserved for bile acids of 100 micromol/L or above, or for lesser elevations complicated by intractable itch, deranged coagulation or a coexisting problem such as pre-eclampsia. Neither the level of 42 micromol/L nor the normal coagulation profile here meets that threshold (Source: RANZCOG: Obstetric cholestasis).

options.text: Treat with topical emollients alone and review her again in four weeks
options.rationale: Emollients and antihistamines address the symptom but a four week interval abandons the surveillance that determines timing of birth, and bile acids can climb into the severe range within days. Symptom relief is part of the plan, not a substitute for it (Source: Royal Women's Hospital Victoria: Intrahepatic cholestasis of pregnancy).
source_refs: Royal Women's Hospital Victoria: Intrahepatic cholestasis of pregnancy

explanation.summary: Itch without a primary rash in the second half of pregnancy, worst on palms and soles and at night, should prompt measurement of serum bile acids and liver transaminases. The diagnosis is important because it is one of the few pregnancy conditions where the timing of birth is chosen on a laboratory number, and the 2021 individual participant data meta analysis reframed practice by showing stillbirth risk rises materially only once peak bile acids reach 100 micromol/L. Ursodeoxycholic acid improves itch and biochemistry but the PITCHES randomised trial found no reduction in adverse perinatal outcomes, so it is offered for symptom control rather than to change the timing plan. Vitamin K is considered when the prothrombin time is prolonged or steatorrhoea is present. Itch and biochemistry resolve within days to weeks after birth, and persistence beyond six weeks warrants hepatology referral.
key_points: Itch of the palms and soles without a primary rash is the classic presentation
Peak bile acids below 100 micromol/L carry near background stillbirth risk
Birth is planned at 38 to 39 weeks for mild disease and 35 to 36 weeks at 100 micromol/L or above
Cardiotocography does not predict the sudden demise associated with this condition
Ursodeoxycholic acid helps the itch but does not improve perinatal outcomes
explanation.pearls: Serum bile acids need not be fasting for diagnosis, but a non fasting sample can run up to about 30 per cent higher than a fasting one, so a borderline non fasting result near 19 micromol/L is worth repeating fasting before committing a woman to a changed birth plan.

sources.label: Royal Women's Hospital Victoria: Intrahepatic cholestasis of pregnancy

subtopic_detail: Involuntary lip and tongue movements emerging in the fourth year of antipsychotic treatment in a woman also taking an anticholinergic
stem:
You are the psychiatry registrar reviewing a 62 year old woman with schizophrenia in a community clinic. She has taken risperidone 4 mg daily for four years, and benztropine 2 mg daily was added in the first month for stiffness and a tremor which settled and has not returned.

Her daughter has noticed over the past four months that her mother is constantly chewing on nothing and that her tongue pushes against the inside of her cheek. On examination there are repetitive lip smacking and tongue rolling movements with occasional finger movements, which stop briefly when you ask her to open her mouth and hold still and which her daughter says are absent while she is asleep. She has no rigidity, her arm swing is symmetrical, and she sits comfortably without shifting or pacing. Her psychotic symptoms have been in remission for three years and she is distressed that people stare at her at the shops.

data_table.Examination: Repetitive lip smacking and tongue rolling with choreiform finger movements, briefly suppressible on request, no cogwheel rigidity, symmetrical arm swing, no truncal restlessness
data_table.Medications: Risperidone 4 mg orally daily for four years, benztropine 2 mg orally daily for four years
data_table.Investigations: Full blood count, urea electrolytes and creatinine, liver function tests, thyroid function and calcium all within normal limits

lead_in: What is the most appropriate next step in her management?

options.text: Increase the benztropine dose to control the abnormal facial movements
options.rationale: Anticholinergics relieve drug induced parkinsonism and acute dystonia but reliably aggravate this movement pattern, so increasing the dose makes the presenting problem worse. The absence of rigidity and the preserved arm swing show there is no parkinsonism left for it to treat (Source: RANZCP: Clinical practice guidelines for schizophrenia).
source_refs: RANZCP: Clinical practice guidelines for schizophrenia

options.text: Add propranolol 10 mg three times daily and review her again in two weeks
options.rationale: Propranolol treats the inner restlessness of akathisia, which is a subjective urge to move relieved by moving, and this woman sits still without pacing or shifting. Treating the wrong movement disorder also leaves the anticholinergic contribution untouched (Source: Therapeutic Guidelines: Psychotropic).

options.text: Increase the risperidone dose to suppress the movements more completely
options.rationale: More dopamine blockade does mask these movements for weeks to months, which is exactly why it is a trap: the underlying receptor supersensitivity worsens and the movements return in a more entrenched form. Dose increases are the classic way a reversible problem is made permanent (Source: RANZCP: Clinical practice guidelines for schizophrenia).
source_refs: RANZCP: Clinical practice guidelines for schizophrenia

options.text: Order a brain MRI and refer to neurology before changing any medication
options.rationale: Structural imaging is warranted when the movements are asymmetrical, progressive, accompanied by cognitive decline or arise without dopamine blocking exposure, none of which applies after four years of an antipsychotic with normal metabolic and thyroid screening. Waiting for imaging also prolongs the exposure that is driving the movements (Source: Therapeutic Guidelines: Psychotropic).

options.text: Cease the benztropine and arrange review of her antipsychotic regimen
options.rationale: Withdrawing the anticholinergic removes a well documented aggravating factor and often produces measurable improvement within weeks, and it is the one change with no psychiatric downside because her parkinsonism resolved years ago. Reviewing the antipsychotic addresses the cause, with a lower dose or a switch to an agent with weaker striatal blockade considered against her three years of remission (Source: RANZCP: Clinical practice guidelines for schizophrenia).
source_refs: RANZCP: Clinical practice guidelines for schizophrenia

explanation.summary: Tardive dyskinesia arises after months to years of dopamine receptor blockade and typically involves the oro bucco lingual region, with choreoathetoid limb and trunk movements in more extensive cases. It is distinguished from akathisia by the absence of a subjective urge to move and from drug induced parkinsonism by the absence of rigidity and bradykinesia, and it characteristically disappears in sleep and can be briefly suppressed voluntarily. Risk rises with age, female sex, longer exposure, diabetes and a history of acute extrapyramidal reactions, and anticholinergic co prescription both worsens established dyskinesia and offers no prophylaxis. Management is exposure reduction where the psychiatric state allows, withdrawal of anticholinergics, and consideration of a vesicular monoamine transporter 2 inhibitor or clozapine in persistent cases. Movements can worsen transiently on dose reduction before improving, which is worth warning the patient about so the change is not abandoned early.
key_points: Suppressible oro bucco lingual movements absent in sleep after prolonged exposure indicate tardive dyskinesia
Anticholinergics worsen tardive dyskinesia and do not prevent it
Raising the antipsychotic dose masks the movements short term and worsens them long term
Absence of rigidity and of subjective restlessness excludes parkinsonism and akathisia
Routine screening with a structured movement scale should occur at least every six to twelve months
explanation.pearls: Movements often flare for four to twelve weeks after the offending antipsychotic is reduced, which is withdrawal emergent dyskinesia rather than treatment failure, so warn the patient in advance and hold the new dose rather than reversing the reduction.

sources.label: RANZCP: Clinical practice guidelines for schizophrenia

subtopic_detail: Acute monoarthritis of the first metatarsophalangeal joint in a man with stage 4 chronic kidney disease
stem:
You are the medical registrar on the acute assessment unit seeing a 68 year old man who woke at 3 am with a hot swollen painful left great toe that he cannot bear to have touched by the bedsheet. He has had two identical episodes in the same joint over the past two years, each settling over about a week.

His background includes stage 4 chronic kidney disease, heart failure with reduced ejection fraction and hypertension, and he takes frusemide 80 mg daily, perindopril, bisoprolol and atorvastatin. On examination the first metatarsophalangeal joint is red, swollen and exquisitely tender with surrounding erythema that fades into normal skin, and there is no skin break, ulcer or lymphangitis. His temperature is 36.8 degrees C and he does not feel systemically unwell. His creatinine is 218 micromol/L with an estimated glomerular filtration rate of 24 mL/min/1.73 m2, and his C reactive protein is 28 mg/L.

data_table.Vital signs: Pulse rate 78 per minute, blood pressure 138/76 mmHg, respiratory rate 16 per minute, SpO2 96 per cent on room air, temperature 36.8 degrees C
data_table.Investigations: Creatinine 218 micromol/L (60-110), estimated glomerular filtration rate 24 mL/min/1.73 m2, urate 0.52 mmol/L (0.20-0.42), C reactive protein 28 mg/L (less than 5), white cell count 9.4 x10^9/L (4.0-11.0)
data_table.Medications: Frusemide 80 mg orally daily, perindopril 5 mg orally daily, bisoprolol 5 mg orally daily, atorvastatin 40 mg orally nightly

lead_in: What is the most appropriate treatment for this episode?

options.text: Start indomethacin 50 mg orally three times daily for five days
options.rationale: Non steroidal anti inflammatory drugs are effective for this presentation but are contraindicated at an estimated glomerular filtration rate of 24 mL/min/1.73 m2, particularly alongside a diuretic and an angiotensin converting enzyme inhibitor, where the combination readily precipitates acute kidney injury. They would be a reasonable first choice if his renal function were normal (Source: Therapeutic Guidelines: Rheumatology).

options.text: Start prednisolone 30 mg orally daily for a five day course
options.rationale: A short high dose oral corticosteroid course is as effective as a non steroidal agent for acute crystal arthritis and is the preferred option when renal impairment closes off both of the alternatives, with no dose adjustment needed for the glomerular filtration rate. The absence of fever, a skin break or systemic upset, together with two prior identical self limiting episodes in the same joint, makes empirical treatment reasonable without deferring for culture (Source: Therapeutic Guidelines: Rheumatology).

options.text: Start colchicine 1 mg orally then 500 mcg one hour later
options.rationale: This is the standard Australian loading schedule but colchicine is renally cleared and the Australian Medicines Handbook advises avoiding it when creatinine clearance falls below 30 mL/min because of accumulation causing myelosuppression and neuromyopathy. It differs from the corticosteroid option chiefly in that its toxicity in this man is dose limiting rather than dose adjustable (Source: Australian Medicines Handbook).

options.text: Start allopurinol 300 mg orally daily and review him in four weeks
options.rationale: Urate lowering therapy does nothing for the acute inflammation and a sudden fall in serum urate can prolong or worsen the attack if started without anti inflammatory cover. It is the right drug at the wrong moment, and the starting dose would also need to be 50 mg daily at this glomerular filtration rate (Source: Australian Medicines Handbook).

options.text: Aspirate the joint and start intravenous flucloxacillin empirically
options.rationale: Septic arthritis is the differential that must not be missed, but it is argued against here by the normal temperature, the intact overlying skin, the normal white cell count and two prior identical episodes that settled without antibiotics. Aspiration of the first metatarsophalangeal joint is also technically difficult and is not required before treating a typical recurrent attack (Source: Therapeutic Guidelines: Antibiotic).

explanation.summary: Acute gout in the setting of advanced chronic kidney disease removes two of the three standard first line treatments, which is why it is a recurring examination scenario and a recurring prescribing error on the wards. Non steroidal agents are contraindicated below an estimated glomerular filtration rate of about 30 mL/min, and colchicine accumulates at the same threshold, leaving systemic corticosteroids or an intra articular injection as the practical choices. Loop diuretics, chronic kidney disease and heart failure all raise serum urate, so this combination of comorbidities makes recurrent attacks predictable. Urate lowering therapy is started once the attack has settled, or during an attack with anti inflammatory cover, and allopurinol is begun at a low dose and titrated to a target serum urate below 0.36 mmol/L. A serum urate measured during an acute attack can be normal or low and never excludes the diagnosis.
key_points: Avoid non steroidal agents and colchicine when estimated glomerular filtration rate is below 30 mL/min
A short oral corticosteroid course is the practical first line in advanced kidney disease
Septic arthritis is excluded clinically here by normal temperature, intact skin and prior identical attacks
Urate lowering therapy does not treat the acute attack and needs anti inflammatory cover if started
Loop diuretics and chronic kidney disease both raise serum urate and drive recurrence
explanation.pearls: Allopurinol is started at 50 mg daily when the estimated glomerular filtration rate is below 30 mL/min and increased by 50 mg every four weeks against the serum urate, since starting at 300 mg in renal impairment is the main risk factor for allopurinol hypersensitivity syndrome.

subtopic_detail: Six weeks of knee pain and a limp in a heavy twelve year old whose knee examination is entirely normal
stem:
You are the emergency department registrar seeing a twelve year old boy brought by his mother with six weeks of left knee pain and a limp that has gradually worsened. He has not fallen or twisted anything, and he plays no organised sport. His mother says he now leans on furniture to get up from the couch and drags the left leg when he walks.

His weight is above the 97th centile for age. The left knee looks normal with a full painless range of movement, no effusion, no joint line tenderness and stable ligaments. When you flex the left hip it rotates obligately into external rotation, and internal rotation of that hip reproduces his pain. He is afebrile, his C reactive protein is 3 mg/L and his white cell count is 7.8 x10^9/L. A radiograph of the left knee taken by his general practitioner two weeks ago was reported as normal.

data_table.Vital signs: Pulse rate 84 per minute, blood pressure 118/70 mmHg, respiratory rate 16 per minute, SpO2 99 per cent on room air, temperature 36.6 degrees C
data_table.Examination: Antalgic gait with the left foot turned out, normal left knee with no effusion or joint line tenderness, obligate external rotation of the left hip on passive flexion, pain on internal rotation of the left hip
data_table.Investigations: C reactive protein 3 mg/L (less than 5), white cell count 7.8 x10^9/L (4.5-13.5), erythrocyte sedimentation rate 8 mm/h (less than 15)

lead_in: What is the most appropriate next step in his management?

options.text: Arrange an MRI of the left knee and review him once the result is available
options.rationale: Cross sectional imaging of a joint with a completely normal examination will be normal, and the finding that matters lies proximal to it. Referred pain along the obturator nerve means knee pain in a child of this age demands examination and imaging of the hip before the knee is investigated further (Source: RCH CPG: Acute limp).

options.text: Arrange an ultrasound of the left hip to look for a joint effusion
options.rationale: Ultrasound answers a different question, distinguishing transient synovitis from septic arthritis in an acutely febrile child with a hip effusion, whereas this boy has six weeks of pain, a normal temperature and normal inflammatory markers. A negative ultrasound would also not exclude the bony displacement that is actually present (Source: RCH CPG: Acute limp).

options.text: Advise simple analgesia and activity modification with review in four weeks
options.rationale: Continued weight bearing over another four weeks risks progression from a stable to an unstable displacement, which raises the rate of avascular necrosis from under 5 per cent to as high as 50 per cent. A gradual six week history is characteristic of the condition rather than reassuring against it (Source: RCH CPG: Slipped capital femoral epiphysis).
source_refs: RCH CPG: Slipped capital femoral epiphysis

options.text: Arrange urgent pelvis radiographs and keep him strictly non weight bearing
options.rationale: Obligate external rotation on hip flexion in an overweight adolescent with weeks of knee pain points to displacement through the proximal femoral physis, and anteroposterior plus frog leg lateral views of the pelvis are the diagnostic test because early slips are visible only on the lateral projection. Non weight bearing is started immediately on clinical suspicion because progression to an unstable slip is the event that destroys the femoral head (Source: RCH CPG: Slipped capital femoral epiphysis).
source_refs: RCH CPG: Slipped capital femoral epiphysis

options.text: Take blood cultures and start intravenous antibiotics for a joint infection
options.rationale: Bone and joint infection is argued against by six weeks of gradual symptoms with a normal temperature, a C reactive protein of 3 mg/L and an erythrocyte sedimentation rate of 8 mm/h. Empirical antibiotics would also delay the imaging and weight bearing restriction that actually change his outcome (Source: RCH CPG: Acute limp).

explanation.summary: Slipped capital femoral epiphysis is the commonest hip disorder of adolescence and its reputation for delayed diagnosis rests almost entirely on referred knee pain, since roughly one in four affected children present complaining only about the knee or distal thigh. Risk factors are obesity, male sex, age around the pubertal growth spurt and endocrinopathy such as hypothyroidism or growth hormone deficiency, and bilateral involvement occurs in about 20 to 40 per cent either at presentation or later. Anteroposterior and frog leg lateral pelvis radiographs are diagnostic, with Klein's line failing to intersect the femoral head on the affected side, and early slips can be invisible on the anteroposterior view alone. Treatment is urgent in situ screw fixation, and the single strongest determinant of outcome is whether the slip is stable at the time of surgery. Avascular necrosis and chondrolysis are the complications that produce lifelong disability.
key_points: Around a quarter of slipped capital femoral epiphysis presents as isolated knee pain
Obligate external rotation on passive hip flexion is the key bedside finding
Anteroposterior plus frog leg lateral pelvis views are required, as early slips hide on the anteroposterior view
Non weight bearing starts on clinical suspicion, before imaging confirms the diagnosis
Normal inflammatory markers over a six week history argue against infection and transient synovitis
explanation.pearls: Klein's line drawn along the superior femoral neck on the anteroposterior view should intersect part of the epiphysis, and any child under about sixteen presenting with knee pain and a limp needs a hip examination before the knee is imaged.

sources.label: RCH CPG: Slipped capital femoral epiphysis
